text: One night he caught Makar digging a tunnel under the prison wall, and Makar whispered, Keep quiet and escape with me, or I will kill you. <break time="0.8s" /> Trembling with anger, Aksionov answered, I have no wish to escape, and you have no need to kill me, for you killed me long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> When the tunnel was discovered, the Governor asked Aksionov, whom he knew to be an honest man, Tell me, before God, who dug the hole. <break time="0.8s" /> His lips and hands trembling, Aksionov asked himself why he should protect the man who had ruined his life. <break time="0.8s" /> But at last he said, It is not Gods will that I should tell, your honor, so do what you like with me. <break time="0.8s" /> That night Makar came to his bed, knelt down, and whispered, Forgive me, Ivan Dmitrich, It was I who killed the merchant and hid the knife. <break time="0.8s" /> When Makar promised to confess so that he could be freed, Aksionov said, I have suffered twenty six years, and now I have nowhere to go. <break time="0.8s" /> Makar began to sob, and hearing him, Aksionov wept too and said, God will forgive you, Maybe I am a hundred times worse than you. <break time="0.8s" /> His heart grew light at these words, and Makar confessed his crime, but by the time the order for his release came, Aksionov was already dead.
